records.name: Germilė
records.facts_used: Germilė: A Lithuanian two-stem name with ger- from geras, good, and mil- from milti, pamilti, to love. This formation continues the Baltic two-part naming model. Its structure should not be confused with the similar-looking foreign name Germanas. Printed page 275 of Daiva Sinkevičiūtė’s 2006 article includes accented Germilė among calendar names that could be recommended for use. This is a particular record of scholarly discussion. The article identifies neither an inventor nor a first birth registration.
records.reason: Exact guide stem explanation and an independently inspected dated scholarly exact-form record.
records.uncertainties: PDF3 printed275 visually checked; accents are stress marks, not alternate vowel letters. Reject unsupported Germanas/germana sister route.

records.name: Santautas
records.facts_used: Santautas is a Lithuanian two-stem name. The guide explains san- through su, kartu, together, and taut- through tauta, people. This preserves the two-part structure characteristic of Baltic personal names without requiring a single modern sentence as its translation. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 collection places Santautas with short form Santas on 25 November. The historical record documents the full and shortened pair in print. The calendar’s date should therefore not be read as the name’s invention date.

The exact spelling Triina appears among Katariina variants in Leili Kuusk’s column in the municipal newspaper Leole, November 2005, page 6. This local printed example records an explanation of the family in Estonia. It is neither a birth-register entry nor the spelling’s earliest known use.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Leole supplies the exact family list, not a secure ultimate Greek etymology. Reject its always-pure gloss. Mägiste is 1929, not 1936; title page checked.
